item.description:
Hold My Notes 1.2.0

  • Note colours of your own: in Settings › General › Note colours, make one with the new colour picker, from soft starter colours, a shading pad, a hue slider or a hex code. They join the five in every note's colour tray, the deck card's Color menu and ⌘. cycling
  • Give a note an emoji with the new button before its title: a grid of everyday ones, a search over all of them, or More emoji… for the Mac's own picker. It shows in All Notes and on the deck, so a note is easy to spot. Settings › Title emoji turns the button off
  • Auto-hide toolbar, in Settings: a note's bottom toolbar fades after 2 seconds unused and the text runs to the bottom of the note. Rest the pointer at the bottom of the note for half a second to bring it back
  • Tables: paste or type a markdown table (a | Name | Role | header over a | --- | --- | row) and it is drawn as a grid, with cells that wrap to fit the note. Click a cell to edit the table's markdown, and it turns back into a grid when the caret leaves
  • Swipe a note into the deck: with an open note, swipe two fingers toward the deck and the note shrinks away into it, closed just as Esc closes it
  • The note's top bar loses its drag handle, leaving the title more room. Drag a note by the empty stretch between its title and its buttons
  • Fixes Hold My Notes icons piling up in the Dock: opening and closing notes quickly could leave a stale icon behind each time, until the Dock was restarted
  • Fixes Chinese, Japanese and Korean typing: a word still being composed with an input method could vanish before you picked its characters
  • Fixes the dashed line on deck cards running through their rounded corners when the deck is on the left of the screen
  • The app now says what Hold My Notes is: a one-time purchase, with no subscription
